# Detection changes and limitations

Saved scene: Assets/Scenes/VR_Warehouse.unity. No clothing state, object tag or fire spawner state is used by inference. Labels depend on image/model evidence.

lying_person was removed from models.json and the scene's model settings. Its original weight file is retained but is no longer loaded or inferred.

The screenshots show `fire2: 2`, not an explicitly named fire class. fire2's checkpoint contains 0–4, Liquid, Metal, Solid, with unknown numeric-class meanings. Both fire2 and the numeric-label person checkpoint still run as diagnostics; their raw predictions and timings remain available but are not accepted semantic detections. No class ID was relabeled. Person candidates instead come from forklift checkpoint's explicitly named class 3 person. This prevents an unidentified numeric result from becoming a misleading fire warning; it does not improve that checkpoint's underlying predictions.

The XR camera's actual stereo projection now supplies the mono detection camera's vertical FOV when stereo is active. When stereo is unavailable, Inspector fallback is 90 degrees. Original XR rendering/tracking is unchanged. Capture is now 960x540, up to 2 requests/sec, with one request in flight and the existing processing-time adaptation. Headset stereo FOV correspondence needs physical Quest verification; the editor validation reported stereo=false and used the fallback.

Person detection uses imgsz 960. nohelmet runs on the full image, then up to four enlarged person/head crops from the same original image. Crop coordinates are translated back to original image coordinates. Predictions touching a crop bottom or outside plausible person-head bounds are rejected; duplicate boxes from the same model are merged. Full names and confidence remain internal. Missing helmet detections never imply nohelmet. Actual nohelmet class-0 detections are associated with explicitly named person boxes.

Fire detection uses its real fire class, first at imgsz 640 and, for weak/missing fire candidates, additionally at imgsz 960. Candidate confidence alone could not distinguish yellow warehouse props from this VFX, so the old high-only threshold was replaced with additional image evidence: warm pixels, plausible shape, and changing candidate pixels after ORB/RANSAC camera-motion alignment. First frames, poor alignment, static yellow regions and unknown class semantics are rejected. This is a conservative heuristic for the current animated VFX, not a newly trained general fire classifier. Rapid head motion/parallax, moving yellow objects, atypical flames, distant or static flame images can still cause errors. No fire-spawner flag is used.

final_verification.json records the final method's comparisons. Twelve existing no-fire warehouse images were evaluated twice each to allow temporal comparison: 0 accepted fire warnings; original baseline had 5 false fire boxes. These are calibration/validation examples, not a held-out benchmark. ForcedFlame/ contains six actual Play JPEG-response pairs with an imported VFX at 1.5 scale, five meters from the camera. Replay with the final method accepted fire on five of those six frames. They cover one enlarged flame condition, not all default random fires or physical fire scenarios. Some distant/default VFX frames still have no model candidates. BareheadFrontal and the user-provided barehead Game screenshot produced nohelmet; the wider YellowHelmetPair still missed the bareheaded worker. The user's yellow-helmet screenshot had no accepted nohelmet result.

Earlier ROI-only probes and size probes are retained to make failed attempts and comparisons reviewable. A full close-view Play run with the new camera and ROI path returned nohelmet and its corresponding person box, while rejecting fire candidates on non-fire warehouse geometry. Final server Play check verified repeated requests and six model timing entries. No lying_person inference occurs.

User UI displays short class names only (No helmet, person, fire, etc.), without model-prefix ambiguity, input previews, confidence, percentages or diagnostic values. Empty results hide it. Raw rejected candidates carry rejection_reason; accepted crop results carry source=person_crop. These fields are internal and available through LatestResult/ResultReceived.

Remaining work for reliable deployment: collect annotated rendered heads at relevant distances/poses and animated fire positives plus yellow-object hard negatives, then evaluate/retrain the respective models. Numeric-label class semantics need the training dataset's labels. Quest display, stereo coverage and performance should be checked in the actual headset.
